_doc: Surviving mutants proven equivalent (no test can distinguish them from the original). Analysis: docs/13_mutation.md. Matched by file + line + operator.

equivalent.why: `self.instance and self.instance.pk` -> `self.instance.pk`: a ModelForm always has an instance (Django creates an empty one), so the first operand is always truthy.

`item and qty > stock` -> `qty > stock`: RequisitionLineItem.item is a non-null FK (on_delete=PROTECT), so `item` is always present for a saved line; the guard is defensive only (also the infeasible MCC row of D2).
`status >= 'sent_back'`: among the 7 valid statuses only 'sent_back' sorts at or after 'sent_back' (s is the highest initial letter), so >= selects exactly the same set as ==.
`status <= 'authorized'`: 'authorized' is the lexicographically smallest valid status, so <= matches only 'authorized'.
Same as S09 (status <= 'authorized' == status == 'authorized' over the valid status domain).
form.save(commit=True) instead of commit=False: the object is saved once more before the final save at the end of form_valid; the end state (fields, notifications) is identical.
Same domain argument as S06 for `status >= 'sent_back'`.
`status is 'sent_back'`: here status was just assigned from the literal in HODActionForm.clean(); CPython interns identifier-like string literals, so identity equals equality on this path.
Same domain argument as S09; the value can only be authorized/sent_back/rejected here.
`qty_issued > 0` -> `!= 0`: negative quantities never reach form_valid (rejected by clean_quantity_issued and the formset validation), so the two conditions agree on every reachable value.
